question:
Create a new KiCad project named b03 in the project directory and draw its schematic for the following request.

Build a NANDO programmer adapter for an AT45DB161D-SU SOIC-8 DataFlash, using the supplied nand_programmator symbol library. Include two 2x7, 2.54 mm programmer sockets. Only the first socket is electrically used in this SPI variant; the second is an unconnected mechanical mating socket.
The first socket uses odd/even pin numbering: 1 = active-low chip select, 2 = SCK, 3 = flash SO/programmer MISO, 4 = flash SI/programmer MOSI, 12 = 3.3 V and 13 = GND. Its remaining pins are unused. Operate the flash from that 3.3 V supply and keep its active-low write-protect and reset inputs inactive. No regulator or level translation is required.
Local dependencies: Use the project-local symbol library in lib/ under the project directory (nand_programmator.kicad_sym); use standard KiCad libraries for everything else.
answer:
Created the [b03 project](./b03.kicad_pro) and its [schematic](./b03.kicad_sch), using the supplied symbol library. J1 carries the requested SPI and power connections; J2 is unconnected. The schematic includes a 100 nF bypass capacitor and a 10 kΩ reset pull-up.

ERC reports **0 errors and 4 symbol-library mismatch warnings**. Footprint libraries were unavailable to the inspection tool, so the assigned footprints—especially the DataFlash SOIC-8 footprint—need verification before layout. The design assumes the programmer supplies 3.3 V.
